almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

amminadab.title: Amminadab
amminadab.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
amminadab.note: Two great lines run back to him. Aaron married his daughter Elisheba, and his son Nahshon stands in David's ancestry, so he sits in both the priestly and the royal genealogies.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

boaz.title: Boaz
boaz.note: A wealthy landowner in Bethlehem, related to Naomi's dead husband Elimelech. He noticed Ruth, the widowed Moabite, gleaning behind his harvesters, and he agreed to act as kinsman-redeemer.

chilion.title: Chilion
chilion.note: Naomi's son. He died in Moab with his father and his brother, and his widow was one of the two left with Naomi when the men were gone.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

elimelech.title: Elimelech
elimelech.note: Naomi's husband. He took the family from Bethlehem to Moab to get away from a famine and died there, and both his sons died after him, which leaves Naomi and Ruth to make the journey back.

ephraimite-2.title: Ephraimite
ephraimite-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ephraimite-2.note: Ruth and 1 Samuel name him twice, and he is a woman from the wilderness years.

hezron.title: Hezron
hezron.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hezron.note: Perez's son, and the line that ends in David runs through him; Ruth closes with it and Matthew picks it up. The same name marks a spot on Judah's southern border, west of Kadesh-barnea.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

leah.title: Leah
leah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
leah.note: Jacob's first wife, given to him by her father Laban in place of Rachel, and Jacob only found out in the morning. He never loved her the way he loved Rachel. Genesis says God gave her children because she was unloved, and she bore six of the twelve sons, Judah among them.

mahlon.title: Mahlon
mahlon.note: Naomi's son, and Ruth's first husband. He died in Moab with his brother and father, which left Ruth a widow with no child before she went back to Bethlehem with Naomi and married Boaz.

mara.title: Mara
mara.note: "Bitter." Naomi came home to Bethlehem from Moab having buried her husband and both sons, and told the women to call her Mara instead, because God had dealt bitterly with her.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

naashon.title: Naashon
naashon.note: Leader of Judah in the wilderness years, and Aaron's brother-in-law. David came from his line, and so does Jesus in Matthew's genealogy.

naomi.title: Naomi
naomi.note: She went to Moab with her husband Elimelech and their two sons during a famine, and all three men died there. Naomi told her Moabite daughters-in-law to go home, but Ruth would not leave her. Her bitterness turned to joy when Ruth married Boaz and had Obed, and Naomi helped raise him like her own.

obed.title: Obed
obed.note: Boaz and Ruth's son, and Naomi helped raise him. He was David's grandfather, which puts Ruth's story inside the royal line.

orpah.title: Orpah
orpah.note: She was Ruth's sister-in-law, a Moabite married to Naomi's son Chilion. When Naomi headed back to Bethlehem, Orpah wept, kissed her, and stayed in Moab.

perez.title: Perez
perez.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
perez.note: Judah's son by Tamar. He pushed out ahead of his twin Zerah, though Zerah's hand had already been marked with a scarlet thread as the firstborn. His line runs through Boaz to David.

rachel.title: Rachel
rachel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rachel.note: Jacob's favourite wife. He was tricked into marrying her older sister Leah first and had to work another seven years for Rachel. For years Leah bore son after son while Rachel had none.

ram.title: Ram
ram.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ram.note: In the line from Judah through Perez to Boaz, and on through Matthew's genealogy to David and Jesus.

ruth.title: Ruth
ruth.note: A Moabite widow who would not leave her mother-in-law Naomi. "Where you go I will go," she said, and went with her to Bethlehem, where she married Naomi's relative Boaz.

salmon.title: Salmon
salmon.note: He was Boaz's father, and his wife was Rahab, the woman who hid Israel's spies at Jericho, which puts him in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus.

tamar-2.title: Tamar
tamar-2.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
tamar-2.note: Judah's daughter-in-law, widowed twice with no heir. Judah held back his third son, so she dressed as a prostitute and conceived twins by Judah himself. He ended up saying she was more righteous than he was, and Ruth 4:12 blesses a family in her name.
